method: Each source on an official Adobe site this session can reach was fetched with curl (default headers, about one request a second) and saved under pages/ with a line in pages/index.tsv. Experience League pages came back as full HTML, so no .md or JSON fallback was needed. Every quote was matched word for word against the saved file with the same matcher idea as handoff/2026-11-17/evidence_page/tools/verify.py (tags stripped, white space and curly quotes normalised). business.adobe.com and aem.live were not tried. To look for pages the research missed, the Experience League and Adobe newsroom site lists (sitemaps) were searched by page address; full-text search of those sites was not available.

records.product: AEM Sites as a Cloud Service
records.assistant: both (Adobe also names Microsoft 365 Copilot as a chat app, and coding tools including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot)
records.what_adobe_says: A client's team can connect Claude or ChatGPT to their AEM as a Cloud Service author environment and then, in plain language, find, create, change, delete and publish pages and content fragments. There are two ways in: a one-click Adobe Experience Manager connector in Claude's connector marketplace (an Adobe Experience Manager plugin in ChatGPT's plugin marketplace), or adding Adobe's single AEM web address by hand. Everything runs under the signed-in person's own AEM permissions. Adobe's own advice is that for changes and deletions, everyday authors should use Adobe's AI Assistant rather than the outside assistant, and that every action that changes content should be reviewed before it is approved.

Adobe offers a unified AEM MCP Server so you can configure a single URL in your chat application or coding agent to get access to a growing set of tools.
Content operations including create, read, update, and delete (CRUD) for pages and content fragments, plus asset importing and assets search (minimum required AEM release version is 26309).

Requests to AEM MCP tools run under the authenticated user's identity, and each tool enforces the user's existing AEM permissions.
For scenarios that modify or delete content, practitioners should use the AI Assistant interface rather than invoking MCP tools directly.
All applications listed under Supported MCP Applications are permitted by default.

Install the Adobe Experience Manager Connector from Anthropic's connector marketplace. It currently has feature parity with Content MCP Server and will expose a growing subset of tools available in AEM's MCP servers.

Install the Adobe Experience Manager plugin from the ChatGPT plugin marketplace. It currently has feature parity with Content MCP Server and will expose a growing subset of tools available in AEM's MCP servers.

Claude users can browse Anthropic's Connector marketplace to 1-click install the Adobe Experience Manager Connector. This MCP server exposes a growing set of tools to interact with AEM, including editing content through prompting.

ChatGPT users can browse OpenAI's Plugin marketplace to 1-click install the Adobe Experience Manager Plugin. This MCP server exposes a growing set of tools to interact with AEM, including editing content through prompting.
These MCP servers include tools for working with Pages, Content Fragments, and Assets, and can be used from the following MCP clients: ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, and Microsoft Copilot Studio.
Use the AEM MCP Server from any AI-powered chat client, such as ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor, to update your website content and publish changes in natural language, no manual editing in the AEM UI.
Enable Developer mode so you can add and configure a custom plugin.
Administrators can also disable access for specific MCP client applications at the organization level if their organization's policies require it.
Always review outputs before applying changes to production content.

wrong_or_unsupported_in_research: Nothing in the record contradicts Adobe. Two things it leaves out matter for a client: Adobe tells everyday authors to use Adobe's own AI Assistant, not the outside assistant, for changes and deletions; and Adobe calls the ChatGPT side a plugin, not a connector.

"Choose access level": the person setting up cannot pick read-only for the whole connection themselves. Adobe's page says the default (read and write) is changed by emailing Adobe. Inside Claude a person can set each tool to always allow, ask or never allow.

"Price shared AEM connector setup once across Sites, Assets and other enabled categories" is the research's own advice, not something an Adobe page says. What Adobe does say is that one web address covers all the categories.
The record's product id aemsites is right. Adobe does not say whether this covers sites built on Edge Delivery Services, so nothing is claimed for that product.

records.product: AEM Edge Functions (AEM Sites, on traditional AEM or Edge Delivery Services)
records.assistant: both, in one sentence, as an example of something a client could build
records.what_adobe_says: This is not a ready-made link to ChatGPT or Claude. AEM Edge Functions lets a client's developers run their own JavaScript on Adobe's managed CDN; it is generally available and approved for production. While it was still a beta program (release notes for January to April 2026) Adobe listed, as one possible use, a client building its own server on it so that assistants like ChatGPT and Claude could reach the client's custom tools. Adobe dropped that line afterwards: the August 2026 notes that announce Edge Functions for everyone repeat the list of uses without it, and today's product page and tutorial do not mention ChatGPT, Claude or such a server. Adobe gives no instructions for it. A partner could offer it as custom development on a generally available building block, but it should not be shown as a connection.

records.product: Workfront Fusion AI modules for AEM, Marketo Engage, Workfront and Fusion
records.assistant: other: OpenAI and Anthropic (Claude) as the AI model behind a Fusion step, chosen with the client's own key; Amazon Bedrock is a third choice. Not the ChatGPT or Claude apps.
records.what_adobe_says: This is not a link to the ChatGPT or Claude apps. Inside Workfront Fusion, four Adobe modules (for AEM, Marketo Engage, Workfront and Fusion itself) take a plain-English instruction and let an AI model carry it out in that Adobe product. By default the model is Adobe's own, with nothing to set up. As an optional, advanced setting, a client can instead supply its own key for OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude) or Amazon Bedrock and pick the model. The client can also limit which read actions and which change-or-delete actions the AI may use. So this supports a line about OpenAI or Anthropic as the AI model behind a Fusion step (with the client's own key); it does not support showing ChatGPT or Claude, the chat apps, as connected to AEM, Marketo Engage or Workfront.

records.product: AEM Cloud Manager and Cloud Migration (parts of Adobe's AEM MCP Server)
records.assistant: neither is named for these two parts. Adobe's pages name ChatGPT and Claude for the shared AEM server as a whole, but describe Cloud Manager and Cloud Migration only for coding tools
records.what_adobe_says: Two more parts of the same Adobe AEM server. Cloud Manager: a client's technical team can look at and manage programs, environments, code repositories and deployment pipelines, and start a pipeline. Cloud Migration: read-only; it fetches the findings of Adobe's Best Practices Analyzer report from Cloud Acceleration Manager so a coding assistant can help move code from AEM 6.x to AEM as a Cloud Service. Every Adobe page that describes either part speaks of a developer's coding tool, not of Claude or ChatGPT chat. That Claude or ChatGPT can reach them is a reading of two facts put together (both parts are in the shared server's table, and both assistants are on its list of supported apps); Adobe does not say it in so many words. The one-click Claude connector and ChatGPT plugin are described as matching the content tools only, so it would mean adding Adobe's web address by hand. Neither Cloud Manager nor Cloud Migration is a product on the tool's canvas.

A 'Content AI MCP Server', described as a companion to the AEM server, lets people search AEM content in plain language. Customers use their own LLM licenses for this capability.'). That is Microsoft's Azure OpenAI service, not ChatGPT, but it is an OpenAI-model link the research's AEM records do not list.

Adobe newsroom, June 2026 ('adobe-accelerates-agentic-ai-adoption', saved as 24b65d16421e.html): 'Now Adobe CX skills and MCP servers are also generally available in Anthropic's Claude Enterprise and Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork'.
